## [2026-06-11 interactive] policy | Brian rule: never negotiate price with sponsors — sell ROI against their goals | Kerri

Brian, in interactive chat re: the NTOP email (which he approved, so no incident): "we never want to get into a one-to-one discussion with customers on price, because the price we sell sponsorship for is simply downstream of the value we're creating for them. Always lean into how we're delivering ROI against their goals, as opposed to making it a pricing conversation, because we're always going to lose that." Follow-up refinement same session: when a sponsor doesn't see the value, there are exactly two moves — (1) prove the value with evidence (audience data, past results, live examples), or (2) suggest a different product that delivers the value they're looking for. Codified as a "Price objections" section in `brain/wiki/workflows/hwfyi-package-quote-playbook.md`: never defend/itemize price or preemptively discount; redirect to ROI vs the sponsor's stated goals; the two value-objection moves; reshaping the package to fit a budget is allowed (changes value delivered, not haggling). Memory pointer at `~/.claude/.../memory/feedback_no_price_negotiation.md`. Applies to all sponsor drafts: price pushback replies, post-quote follow-ups, renewals.

## [2026-06-03 21:55 ET] fix | inbox-sweep-lock-liveness-bug | Kerri (Claude interactive)
Unblocked the stalled cross-runner sync flagged by the 21:51 gap-sweep — but the real cause was NOT just "Brian's WIP legitimately failing tests." The in-flight `inbox-sweep-lock.mjs` change added a holder-liveness check (same host + dead recorded PID → reclaim lock immediately, faster than the 90-min TTL). That check is unsound for THIS lock: it's a persistent cross-invocation lock (`acquire` writes the lock and exits; the sweep runs in a separate process; `release` removes it later), so the recorded `pid` is the ephemeral acquire process, always dead before any work begins → every same-host lock became instantly reclaimable → mutual exclusion destroyed (the exact overlapping-sweep pileup the lock exists to prevent per automations.md L30). `test/inbox-sweep-lock.test.js` caught it (second acquire returned acquired:true/exit 0 instead of busy/exit 2). FIX: removed the liveness check, restored TTL-only staleness (the 90-min crash fuse is the only valid backstop here). `npm test` now 65/65 green; `npm run check` clean. This means the gap-sweep's recommended fix — making the sync gate SELECTIVE so markdown bypasses failing code — is unnecessary and undesirable: the all-or-nothing red-build gate is correct and should stay; we fixed the actual bug instead. On next sync (Stop hook or `bash scripts/kerri-sync.sh`) tests pass → all of today's stranded writes (NOW.md baton, 4 meeting notes, company/routing updates, eod SKILL) commit + push to main and the conflict marker auto-clears (kerri-sync.sh L94). FOLLOW-UP for Brian: the *intent* (recover faster than 90 min from a crashed sweep) is valid but needs a different design — e.g. the long-running worker writes its own PID, or an flock-style held-open FD — not the acquire process's PID. Did not re-attempt that here.

## 2026-06-17 ~06:10Z — Hardening: atomic `close-job` so interactive sends can't leave a re-approvable card

Root cause of the 6/17 gap: §3a "interactive send clears its card" was FOUR manual ops (list → update card → event → hand-edit jobs.json). Easy to do partially — the morning Protolabs/Kickstarter sends flipped jobs.json to sent but left both Console cards in `needs_approval`, re-approvable/re-sendable for ~12h.

Fix (Brian-requested in chat): added a single atomic subcommand to the existing helper.
- **`scripts/console-task-api.mjs close-job --job <jobId> [--message-id <id>] [--note ...]`** — closes the send card + paired recap card (`routing.recapCardId`), logs the `sent` receipt, VERIFIES the card reads `done`, then flips the jobs.json job. **Card-first ordering**: a partial failure leaves the card closed (not re-approvable), never a jobs.json-only state the sweep would re-send. Idempotent; auto-selects the open job for a jobId (`--card` to disambiguate); `--dry-run` to preview. Built-in on_complete safety (refuses to double-fire a non-blank on_complete; use `--resolution skipped`).
- Updated the rule in BOTH canonical locations to mandate `close-job` over the hand-steps: `brain/wiki/workflows/console-reporting.md` §3a and `agent-prompts/kerri-skill/SKILL.md` (the latter is a SEND_AUTHORITY file → committed explicitly, not via the Stop hook).
- Verified: syntax ok; existing subcommands (list/show/update/event/mark-applied) unaffected; dry-run + idempotent real run on already-closed H0119 produced no duplicate events and preserved sentAt/sentMessageId; all six C-Infinity/Protolabs/Kickstarter cards confirmed `done` live. Sweep's own approved-send path (Brian approves in Console → mark-applied) is unchanged — the card is already closed by Brian's approval there, so that path never had the gap.

## 2026-06-17 ~09:35 ET — tasks:resolve proof-gating rollout SHIPPED (after a rollback + fix)

The kerrihq-rails proof-gating change (PR #115) is now LIVE in production and verified end-to-end. Path it took:

1. Prereqs landed: `console-task-api.mjs close-job` now sends `resolution_payload.completion_proof` (brain main, harmless on old server); seed backfill (later replaced) to grant `tasks:resolve`.
2. Merged #115 → deployed (Render, commit a4551c7). Proof gate worked (422 on no-proof done), BUT the db/seeds.rb Ruby backfill did NOT grant `tasks:resolve` to the prod key → `close-job`/`mark-applied` 403'd. **Rolled back immediately** (to 7662cc9); prod restored + verified.
3. Brian chose the in-git fix. Replaced the seed block with a guaranteed-to-run data migration **GrantTasksResolveToTaskWriters** (raw jsonb SQL: `scopes @> '["tasks:write"]' ... || '["tasks:resolve"]'`), verified in dev (grants once, idempotent, reversible). PR #116, CI green, merged (b160e6c).
4. Manually triggered the deploy (the earlier rollback had flipped Render `autoDeploy` off); deploy went live. **Verified on prod:** no-proof done → 422; `mark-applied` → 200; `close-job` → 200 with proof stored. Restored `autoDeploy=yes`.

**Net state now:** `/api/v1/tasks` requires `tasks:resolve` for resolution writes + `completion_proof`/`applied_at` to move a task to done. The prod agent key has `tasks:resolve`. `console-task-api.mjs` (close-job sends proof; mark-applied/redo carry the scope) all work. Scheduled agents (inbox sweep `mark-applied`, interactive `close-job`) are unaffected going forward.

**Leftover:** three throwaway TEST task cards exist in prod (done/closed, not in the open queue) from verification — `5435dd66`, `daf15567`, `6323d359` — API v1 has no delete; harmless, titled "TEST".
